findings.summary: The printTestInputs guard is still a substring match, and the drift fixtures ADDED BY THIS COMMIT satisfy the settings.gradle.kts check on their own. Deleting the rootSettings declaration leaves the guard green -- the same blindness as the grep it replaced, on the same input.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified in a copy of this tree: removed the three-line inputs.file(rootDir.parentFile.resolve("settings.gradle.kts")) hunk from buildSrc/build.gradle.kts, ran ./gradlew -p buildSrc -q printTestInputs. The root settings file is gone from the 785-line list, but three paths remain -- buildSrc/src/test/resources/drift-fixtures/{clean,missing-build-file,missing-settings-entry}/settings.gradle.kts, declared by the javaFixtures inputs.dir. Replaying the exact `case "$_declared" in *"$_want"*` loop gives PASS java_tests.py / PASS check-module.sh / PASS settings.gradle.kts, FAILED=0. So a developer who reverts the rootSettings declaration gets `ok N harness test(s) pass` while `test` is UP-TO-DATE across a module rename -- the one change RuleListTest, ModulePlanTest and ModuleListDerivationTest exist to catch. Fix: compare whole lines for equality against "$ROOT/settings.gradle.kts", "$ROOT/scripts/java_tests.py", "$ROOT/scripts/check-module.sh" -- a `while IFS= read -r l` over a here-string keeps it pipe-free and SIGPIPE-free.

findings.summary: afterEvaluate resolves :buildSrc:testRuntimeClasspath during configuration of EVERY build, not only when printTestInputs is asked for. A diagnostic for one gate is now paid, and can now fail, on every Gradle invocation in the repository.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified in a copy: added an unresolvable `testImplementation("does.not.exist:probe:1.0")` to buildSrc and ran `./gradlew --offline help` at the ROOT. It fails with "A problem occurred configuring project ':buildSrc' > Could not resolve all files for configuration ':buildSrc:testRuntimeClasspath'" -- a root task that needs nothing from buildSrc's test classpath. Concretely: a harness test-only dependency that cannot be resolved (repository outage, --offline, partially warmed CI cache) now breaks `./gradlew :format:build`, and each of the 24 gradlew invocations check-module.sh makes at GATE_SCOPE=full pays a configuration-time resolution it does not need. This is the answer to "sound or merely working": it works, and it is not confined to the task it serves. Confine it -- dereference `tasks.named<Test>("test")` inside doLast (a TaskProvider captured in an action closure carries no task dependency, so the 47 s problem does not return), or gate the afterEvaluate on the task actually being requested.

findings.summary: printTestInputs is configuration-cache incompatible, and org.gradle.configuration-cache=true is already set in the root gradle.properties; it only escapes today because `-p buildSrc` reads properties from buildSrc, not the root. The gate discards the reason.
findings.failure_scenario: `./gradlew -p buildSrc printTestInputs --configuration-cache` fails: "Task `:printTestInputs` of type `org.gradle.api.DefaultTask`: cannot serialize Gradle script object references" -- the doLast lambda captures the script-level `declaredTestInputs`. The day someone adds buildSrc/gradle.properties (which build.md's memory caps arguably already want, since `-p buildSrc` never reads the root's org.gradle.jvmargs) or sets configuration-cache in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties, every commit touching scripts/ or buildSrc/ is blocked by `could not read the test task's declared inputs (printTestInputs)` with the cause sent to /dev/null by line 44. Keep stderr in .harness/, as the sibling gradlew call on line 64 already does.

findings.summary: M0.6 is "wire check-module.sh into .pre-commit-config.yaml and CI". Only the pre-commit half is delivered; the CI half becomes prose in M0.7's row and a present-tense claim in AGENTS.md.
findings.failure_scenario: There is no .github/ in the tree, so nothing sets GATE_SCOPE=full and the AGENTS.md row added by this commit -- "CI sets GATE_SCOPE=full to build all eight" -- is a statement about a file that does not exist. Defensible (M0.7 owns the workflow), but the M0.6 row itself records no split, so a reader reconciling the backlog against the tree cannot tell the CI half was deliberately deferred rather than forgotten. One clause on the M0.6 row fixes it.
